name: Fastmail
summary: Private, ad-free email hosting with your own domain. Fast, secure email, calendars and contacts from an independent provider that doesn't mine your data. From 1 August 2026 you pick EU (Amsterdam) or US data residency, encrypted at rest on Fastmail's own servers — note that EU data is initially still replicated and backed up to the US while that infrastructure matures.
best_for: individuals and small businesses that want fast, private, ad-free email on their own domain with proper support and masked-email aliases
skip_if: your team lives in Google Docs/Drive collaboration (Workspace bundles that), or free mail genuinely serves you and privacy isn't a priority
honest_knock: You're paying for what the free giants monetize differently: no ads, no profiling, real support and standards-first email (JMAP/IMAP everywhere). The honest limits: it's email/calendar/contacts, not a Workspace-style office suite, so document collaboration lives elsewhere, and migrating decades of Gmail habits (filters, integrations) takes a weekend of care. For owning your address on your own domain, it's the boring, excellent choice.

pricing.entry_price_terms: Individual · per month, or $60 for twelve months, with 60 GB for one person
pricing.notes: (read 2026-08-26 on fastmail.com/pricing over a US connection, with their country selector on United States and the 12-month term chosen; re-read 2026-09-29 from a Dutch connection, where the page serves euros with the same numerals and an unchanged 1-, 12-, 24- and 36-month ladder) Individual is $5 a month, or $60 for twelve months, with 60 GB of storage for one person. Duo is $8 a month ($96 a year) for two inboxes and 120 GB. Family is $11 a month ($132 a year) for up to six people and up to 360 GB, at 60 GB each. The page also sells 24- and 36-month terms, so the twelve-month figure is the middle of three commitments rather than the cheapest one.

compare_with.name: Proton Mail or Google Workspace
compare_with.why: Proton leads on E2EE, Workspace on suite breadth — Fastmail wins on speed, standards support and price for pure email
